note: Round 5, breadth first. The goal is more distinct n with a real result, not shaving existing records. The richest unexplored area is n = 82–100: all 19 share one product bound (3.707), and 82 = 81-grid + 1 is the exact analogue of 17 = 16-grid + 1, which beat its product bound by 0.13. If 82 falls, 83, 84, … can each be grown into their own value. Large n is slow, so those tasks get 12–15 minutes. The cheap 28→35 chain stays on short tasks.
insights: Records so far: 17 (2.5784), 26 (2.9506), 27 (2.9512). Every one came from "grow" (best (n−1) packing + 1 cube) or "best" restarts.
Long searches pay off while a record is still falling: n = 27 went 2.9818 → 2.9512 in one 10-minute run.
One minute is useless for n ≥ ~50: the search doesn't even reach a valid packing in that time. Each step costs ~n² pair checks.
Top-down shots below s = 3 at n = 40 or 60 look hopeless for now. Even in 3D, nothing above 14 cubes fits below 3.
I believe n = 18–25 need ≈2.707 (no movement in ~30 min of search). In 2D, 5 squares get a cheap trick but 6 need side 3.
